relevance_note: The paper describes two patients with TNFAIP3 variants in detail ("Herein, we report two children with the primary presentation of HLH, with a mutation in TNFAIP3, in favor of HA20") and summarises earlier-published HA20/TNFAIP3 patients individually.
method_note: Read the whole paper (no supplementary section present). Values were entered by hand into a Python builder script in my scratch directory; the script only resolved typed spans to the paper's exact characters (thin spaces U+2009, curly apostrophes) and assembled the JSON, then a check confirmed every span occurs verbatim. Scope: 9 individuals. (1) The two first-hand patients, labelled by their section headings 'Patient one' and 'Patient two' (the paper also calls them 'our first/second patient' and, in Table 3, 'Our patient N. 1/2'). (2) The parents of Patient two, tested negative by trio WES and Sanger ('his parents are homozygous wild type'); the paper names them only jointly as 'parents', so they are labelled 'mother of Patient two' and 'father of Patient two', with sex left 'not reported'. (3) Two previously published patients in the Table 3 literature summary. The table's 'Number' column is treated as a row index, not a person label, so they are 'Table 3 row 1' (Li et al. [29]) and 'Table 3 row 2' (Takagi et al. [9]). Each is also described in the Discussion text, and those details are merged into the same row because they are clearly the same person within this paper (same author, sex, age and HLH/MAS features). (4) The three patients of Zhang et al. [25], each described individually in the Discussion ('ref [25] patient', '... 2', '... 3'). They are included because the paragraph presents them as HA20 patients, but the paper gives them no explicit diagnosis label or variant, so disease_label is 'not reported' and they have no variant rows. Out of scope: Patient one's healthy older sister and his consanguineous parents, who were neither tested nor affected; the other three Li et al. patients, mentioned only as a count. Age choices: for Patient one, age at diagnosis is the age at genetic HA20 diagnosis (2 years and 4 months, when WES results were delivered); his HLH was diagnosed at 4 months, which is also Table 3's 'Age at onset'. For Patient two, age at diagnosis is not stated. His last follow-up is given only as time since onset ('4 years have passed since the first presentation of the disease'), not as an age, so age_at_last_evaluation is 'not reported'. Patient one's age at death is not stated (some time after 2 years 4 months). is_proband is null for the patients because the paper uses neither 'proband' nor 'index case' and this is a two-patient report. Group statements: 'Both of our patients met ... criteria of MAS', 'Our patients did not have any symptoms of Behcet's-like or other autoimmune disorders' and 'we did not find any positive autoantibodies ... in our patients' name the group explicitly (both first-hand patients), so they are used with evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement'. The Behcet's-like/autoimmune statement does not name specific features, so it was not used to exclude individual checklist items such as oral ulcers. Checklist judgments: 'intermittent fever' was counted as recurrent fever, but a single prolonged fever or a plain 'fever' was not. HLH-related pancytopenia was not counted as 'cytopenia (autoimmune)'; Zhang patient 2's autoimmune hemolytic anemia was. Patient one's cerebral hemorrhage with coma was counted as central nervous system involvement. Patient two's 'The skin appeared normal' was taken to exclude skin lesions. Table 3 '-' cells in 'Other features' for the first-hand patients are undefined, so they were treated as not reported. Contradictions and oddities: (a) Patient two's protein change is printed 'p. L275P' (leucine to proline) but described in the text as 'a proline to leucine amino acid change'; recorded as printed. (b) Patient one: the text says 'He had normal ESR, CRP', but Table 1 lists ESR 11 (range 0-10) and CRP 6 (<6), which are borderline. The text statement was used (excluded). (c) Patient one: the Case presentations section says the HLH criteria were met, while the Discussion says 'all five HLH criteria were not met in the first patient' (hemoglobin 9.2 vs threshold 9 g/dl). (d) The Li et al. variant is printed 'c.259C > T (p.R87X)' (transcript NM_006290) in the text and 'c.C259T, p.R87X' in Table 3. One variant row uses the text form. (e) For the Takagi patient, the text says 'de novo mutation of TNFAIP3 was detected' without a parental-testing statement, so inheritance is 'not reported' under rule 8. The text says 'pancytopenia' and Table 3 'thrombocytopenia'. (f) For Patient two, the text says 'familial HLH (FHL) was confirmed' before WES, which conflicts with the later HA20 diagnosis; the Background speaks of 'a case' although two are reported. (g) Patient two's '6q23.3' is a cytoband, not genomic coordinates, so genomic_coordinates is null. The CADD score of 29.1 and the SIFT/PolyPhen-2 predictions are in silico results, not functional assays, so functional_evidence is 'not reported' and the prediction is recorded under pathogenicity. Laboratory abnormalities were taken from Tables 1 and 2 only as severity details, or where the value lies well outside the printed normal range and the text corroborates it (Patient two's ESR/CRP 'returned to normal values'). Table 1/2 asterisks are defined as 'laboratory changes in favor of HLH'.
